accepted25UnitAssessments.assessment: I read the complete Chinese and proposed English, preceded by b11 and followed by b13–14. The five altered unit words still denote the oil offered by the few catties, forty-eight catties of oil, one catty of wick-rushes, twenty-four catties of oil and five catties. The final three and one remain an intelligible ellipsis under the same unit. The donor ranks, vat-sized lamp, incessant burning and promised protection have not changed. This expresses the source quantities without converting them or claiming a modern standard weight.

The passage still moves from Mother Ma’s assurance that it costs very little to conspicuously wealthy donors and a lamp almost the size of a vat. Grandmother Jia’s practical question separates the pious pitch from its expense. Catty/catties sits naturally in that concrete list and does not explain away the irony, add a narrator’s condemnation, or change the open speech carried into b13. The flattering living Bodhisattvas and the claimed divine protection remain Mother Ma’s rhetoric.

The current bounded mass rule applies to this specific unit: one catty is singular and the other four changed tokens are catties. Jintian is a name and is untouched. The entire Chinese, numbers, segmentation and all non-unit wording match the B10 body; only these five unit tokens differ. The terminology now agrees with the selected chapter53 mass list without imposing a global replacement on other jin uses. The old three reviews remain valid only for the old content hash and are preserved in the authenticated B10 context.

I read the complete Chinese and English in the b11–14 sequence. Four taels or half a catty remains a range of small offerings, not an equation or an assertion that four taels equals half a catty. The seven-catties maximum, five-at-least ellipsis, decision on five catties each day and collection of a month’s allowance all retain their distinct meanings. The later strings of cash are alms, not oil weights. Exactly half a jin, seven jin and five jin change their unit words; no amount, speaker, source text or other phrase changes.

Mother Ma’s apparent restraint remains a persuasive turn: she first allows poor donors less, then warns that excessive offerings might harm Bao-yu’s blessings, and Grandmother Jia settles a daily allowance. Her intoned invocation and the move toward Aunt Zhao’s scraps in b14 keep the contrast between piety and acquisition visible without an added moral label. The three unit substitutions do not interrupt the give-and-take or make the period dialogue sound like a modern financial calculation.

Half a catty takes the singular; seven catties and five catties take the plural. The customary mass term stays distinct from taels of oil and from the later cash allowance. No metric conversion, modern weight equivalence, new note or retroactive assertion that jin was wrong is introduced. This unit and b12 are the entire accepted-content exception. Its replacement review records must bind the new current hash, while the original three records and the old batch21–25 checkpoint remain historical evidence, not approvals of changed text.
